correctness.rationale: For the repaired fixed p=(1,15,16)/32 finding, each occupancy triple has integer numerator equal to its multinomial coefficient times its product of integer masses, over 32^n. Summing the first and mixed moments of the two counts gives the covariance as an exact fraction. The four fractions in the repair were reproduced independently by summing over ordered allocations; their signs imply at least one reversal between each consecutive pair of checkpoints when zero terms are ignored. At n=3 with two positive-probability boxes, both counts coincide with the nonconstant split-(1,2) indicator, so covariance is positive. At n>3 they cannot both be positive but each has positive expectation, so covariance is strictly negative. For a one-point support the counts are deterministic. Hence three boxes is minimal over n>=3.
residual_risks: Only the stated lower bound and the minimal number of boxes for this pair of loads are claimed. No assertion about an exact total switch count or a universal bound for unequal probabilities.

value.rationale: The example disproves a natural extension of an exact uniform one-positive-interval law, at the fewest boxes allowing the obstruction for the two stated occupancy sizes. A single exact fixed distribution and separated positive checkpoints provide a reusable benchmark for heterogeneous occupancy reasoning. The finding is not just an unmotivated covariance calculation.
residual_risks: Does not characterize how widespread the nonuniform behavior is or give a general test for it.
